title: Rhombus_Botnet_Investigation_3fc
description: Investigate and identify the source of unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation in the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and performance degradation, indicative of a potential botnet infection. Your task is to investigate and identify the source of these issues, which may include suspicious services and abnormal network traffic. The malware family involved is Rhombus.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external host? The flag is the service name.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, check the systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is named `system-update-checker.service`. The flag is `system-update-checker.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services are managed by the systemd init system. You can list all services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. Look for any unusual or recently created services. Try using `systemctl status <service-name>` to inspect a specific service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. The suspicious service is named `system-update-checker.service`. Use `systemctl status system-update-checker.service` to verify it.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating the abnormal network traffic? The flag is the service name.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. The service generating abnormal network traffic is named `network-diagnostics-probe.service`. The flag is `network-diagnostics-probe.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services are managed by the systemd init system. You can list all services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`.

hints.title: Directional Hint

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service? The flag is the timer name.
levels.solution: Investigate the systemd timers using the command `systemctl list-timers` and look for any timers associated with the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism is named `system-update-checker.timer`. The flag is `system-update-checker.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers are used to schedule systemd services. You can list all timers using the command `systemctl list-timers`.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. Look for any timers associated with the suspicious service. Try using `systemctl status <timer-name>` to inspect a specific timer.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. The persistence mechanism is named `system-update-checker.timer`. Use `systemctl status system-update-checker.timer` to verify it.
